summary: Independent LLM review of the exact frozen candidate c232c07c1cce4b3a approves its stated scoped theorem and complete argument. Thus normalized retained simplex capacity is upper semicontinuous, which makes the capacity-at-least-c constraint closed. The infimum is an attained strictly positive minimum when the class is nonempty. The explicit empty-class branch is harmless and does not introduce an assumed stability theorem. Hence every missed simplex contains its centroid in its interior. The own retained-centroid cap and full missed weight give exactly [1-q(q-delta_d)v]/2, with strict inequality in the descendant branch. The entering facets are precisely those with u dot grad(lambda_i)>0. Their projections cover the simplex projection with disjoint interiors outside null boundaries; facets parallel to u project to lower dimension. The projection Jacobian and facet-area formula give projection area=d volume times s, hence volume=(L/d) times projection area with the correct sign. The base-fixing shear has determinant one and can place the apex projection in the base. Every frustum projection then lies in the base. Its height is H/(d+1), and the chord-projection identity yields the exact upper bound |B|/(d+1). With a simplex base, taking the full base and any top-face point attains the bound. The classical sharp centroid-cap equality has the apex-side orientation. A missed simplex lies in the retained frustum and obeys the capacity bound. At d>=3 and v=beta/q, q/2>1/(d+1), so no sharp ordinary cap can miss a qualifying source. This is correctly scoped as an equality obstruction, not a quantitative general cap surplus.
